dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified grid supplies a nonempty family of measurable, pairwise disjoint regions partitioning its stored domain.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second projection of the grid, giving its function from cells to subsets of Point.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: Universally quantify types Cell, Point, and Parameter, with no specified cardinalities or dimensions.
Equip Point with a measurable-space structure and Parameter with a normed additive commutative group, a compatible real normed-space structure, and completeness for its induced uniform structure.
Universally quantify a grid on Cell and Point, a measure μ = physicalVolume on Point, and a field f = materialParameter : Point → Parameter.
After the hypotheses, existentially quantify a single assignment a : Cell → Parameter. It may depend on the preceding structures, grid, measure, and field.
In the first conclusion universally quantify c : Cell; in the uniqueness clause universally quantify b : Cell → Parameter.
In the locality clause universally quantify c : Cell and g : Point → Parameter after a has been selected.
In the constant-field clause universally quantify c : Cell and p : Parameter after a has been selected.
hypotheses: The grid carries a domain Ω and regions R(c), with Cell nonempty, every R(c) measurable, distinct cells having disjoint regions, and x ∈ Ω if and only if there exists c with x ∈ R(c).
For every cell c, μ(R(c)) ≠ ∞. Together with the preceding condition, every region has finite positive measure.
For every cell c, MeasureTheory.Integrable f (μ.restrict R(c)) holds.
conclusions: There exists a : Cell → Parameter such that for every c, μ(R(c)) ≠ 0, μ(R(c)) ≠ ∞, f is integrable with respect to μ.restrict R(c), and a(c) = Aμ,R(c)(f).
For every b : Cell → Parameter, if for every c the same nonzero-measure, finite-measure, integrability, and equality-to-Aμ,R(c)(f) conditions hold for b(c), then b = a as functions.
For every c and every g : Point → Parameter, if f(x) = g(x) for all x ∈ R(c), then a(c) = Aμ,R(c)(g).
For every c and every p : Parameter, Aμ,R(c)(x ↦ p) = p. This clause concerns the averaging operator on constant fields and does not assert that the original field f is constant.
mathematical_definitions: Write mR = (μ(R)).toReal and I(ν,h) = MeasureTheory.integral ν h. Define Aμ,R(h) = mR⁻¹ • I(μ.restrict R,h), where • is real scalar multiplication on Parameter.
LocalDef003 μ R h q is exactly the conjunction μ(R) ≠ 0, μ(R) ≠ ∞, MeasureTheory.Integrable h (μ.restrict R), and q = Aμ,R(h).
Under the usual meanings of measure restriction and the Bochner integral, Aμ,R(h) is the normalized integral (1/μ(R)) • ∫R h dμ, with μ(R) regarded as a real number for finite-measure regions.
Pointwise agreement on R means ∀ x ∈ R, f(x) = g(x); equality of assignments means equality at every cell.
The normed-space and completeness assumptions make Parameter a real Banach space.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any measurable space of points, real Banach space of parameter values, and grid consisting of a nonempty family of measurable, pairwise disjoint regions covering its domain exactly, let μ be a measure and f a parameter-valued field. Suppose each cell region has finite positive μ-measure and f is integrable with respect to the measure restricted to that region. Then there is a unique assignment of a parameter value to every cell satisfying the validity predicate: each value is the inverse real region measure times the specified integral of f over that region. The same assignment also has this locality property: replacing f by any field that agrees with it at every point of a chosen region leaves that region's computed value equal to its assigned value. Moreover, averaging any globally constant parameter-valued field over any cell returns that constant. The normalized-integral description uses the usual interpretation of the integration and restriction operations; their underlying implementations are not fully exposed in the packet.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: An existing grid requires a nonempty Cell type. Empty-index vacuity is therefore excluded, but for types admitting no grid the universal quantification over grid instances has no instances.
The implication makes no assertion for a grid and measure with any zero-measure or infinite-measure cell, or for a field failing integrability on any cell.
Finite positive cell measures force each cell region to be nonempty; together with the nonempty cell type this forces the grid domain and Point to be nonempty whenever the hypotheses hold.
Cell need not be finite or countable. Neither μ(Point) nor μ(Ω) is required to be finite, and global integrability of f is not assumed.
The grid has exact disjointness, not disjointness modulo null sets. No Euclidean geometry, cell shape, mesh size, regularity, or adjacency is encoded.
Parameter need not be scalar-valued or finite-dimensional, and may be the trivial real Banach space. No order, positivity, or physical admissibility condition on its values is encoded.

The alternative field g has no separate global measurability or integrability hypothesis. Its condition is exact pointwise agreement on the selected region; no claim with merely almost-everywhere agreement is explicitly stated.
The witness a is selected before quantifying alternative fields and constants, so one assignment must satisfy every locality instance.
The final constant-field identity does not depend on a and does not say a(c) = p unless the original field has the corresponding agreement with that constant.
No error bound, convergence under refinement, reconstruction on Point, numerical approximation, or conservation identity is separately asserted.
The average formula is a total Lean expression even outside the hypotheses, but the theorem supplies no zero-volume, infinite-volume, or nonintegrable-field guarantee.
ambiguities: D047 exposes only MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1. Its type and owner module indicate the intended Bochner-integral role, but the supplied body alone does not determine integration semantics. The exact translation can therefore retain this as the operation I; identifying it unconditionally with the mathematical Bochner integral requires the omitted definition or its specification.

D046 delegates restriction to the unexpanded operation MeasureTheory.Measure.restrictₗ, and D013 delegates integrability to the unexpanded predicate MeasureTheory.Integrable. Their standard measure-theoretic interpretations are used descriptively, but their defining laws are not independently recoverable from the displayed bodies.

Several foundational external-frontier structures are supplied only by type, and some conversion and algebra operations delegate to unexpanded definitions or inferred instances. The translation uses their conventional mathematical meanings; the packet is not a fully expanded foundational specification.
